chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'We, the assembly of angels, do not enter a house in which there is a dog, or a statue of a body, or a vessel in which urine is passed.'

key_terms.إِنَاءٌ يُبَالَ فِيهِ: vessel in which urine is passed

ai.seo_question: What three things prevent angels from entering a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the spiritual purity required in domestic spaces, linking the presence of these three impurities to the withholding of angelic blessings. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the ritual and spiritual consequences of keeping dogs (outside for work) and displaying statues, while also clarifying the specific nature of the 'vessel' as one used for urination rather than general waste. It underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining a sanctified environment conducive to divine presence.
